question.text: An ellipse <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> passes through the vertices of the hyperbola <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi><mo>:</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>49</mn></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>64</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Let the major and minor axes of the ellipse <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> coincide with the transverse and conjugate axes of the hyperbola <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi></math>. Let the product of the eccentricities of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>l</mi></math> is the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>113</mn><mi>l</mi></math> is equal to _______.

solution.text:
Given,

Hyperbola:y264-x249=1

And ellipse E:x2a2+y2b2=1 passes through the vertices of the hyperbola H:x249-y264=-1, so vertices will be V≡0,±8

So b2=64

Now eccentricity of hyperbola will be eH=1+a2b2=1+4964

And eccentricity of ellipse x2a2+y2b2=1 will be

eE=1-a2b2=1-a264

And using b=8

We get, eH×eE=12 (given)

⇒1-a264×1138=12

⇒64-a2×113=32

⇒64-a2=322113

⇒a2=64-322113

Now length of latus rectum will be l=2a2b=2864-322113=1552113

⇒113l=1552
